references.text: The command to help a poor brother who has become destitute and not let him perish reflects the same principle of generosity toward needy Israelites.
The continuation of the same text emphasizes that there will always be poor people in the land, and therefore one must be open-handed toward those in need.
He who shuts his ear to the cry of the poor shall himself call out without receiving an answer—a wisdom warning against hardening one's heart toward the poor.
He who gives to the poor will lack nothing, but he who shuts his eyes will receive many curses.
The prophet's call to share bread with the hungry and bring the homeless into one's house shows the same concern for the poor.
John asks how God's love can be in anyone who has worldly goods and sees a brother in need yet hardens their heart toward him—a direct parallel to not hardening one's heart.
James warns against dismissing a brother or sister who lacks clothing and food with mere words, without giving them what they truly need.
